subject: Economics
description: Covers Mahalanobis model, Plan Holidays, Rolling Plan, Gadgil Formula, and specific plan themes.

questions.stem: The Second Five Year Plan (1956-61) of India was based on which economic model?

options.option_text: Mahalanobis Model — focusing on rapid industrialization and heavy industries
Harrod-Domar Model — focusing on agriculture and irrigation
Gadgil Strategy — focusing on balanced regional development
Rao-Manmohan Model — focusing on economic liberalization

questions.explanation: SECOND PLAN (1956-61): Drafted under the leadership of P.C. Mahalanobis. It shifted the focus from agriculture (First Plan) to RAPID INDUSTRIALIZATION, specifically heavy and basic industries (steel, machinery). It advocated a dominant role for the public sector. Three major steel plants (Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela) were established during this plan. The First Plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model. PYQ FREQUENCY: Highly repeated in SSC and State PSCs.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: During which period did India observe "Plan Holidays", abandoning the Five-Year Plan structure temporarily in favour of Annual Plans?

options.option_text: 1966-1969 — following the Indo-Pak war, severe droughts, and devaluation of the rupee
1978-1980 — during the tenure of the Janata Party government
1990-1992 — during the balance of payments crisis and economic reforms
1962-1965 — during and after the Sino-Indian war

questions.explanation: PLAN HOLIDAYS (1966-1969): After the miserable failure of the Third Plan (due to the 1962 Sino-Indian War, 1965 Indo-Pak War, and severe droughts in 1965-66), the government lacked resources to launch the Fourth Plan. Instead, three Annual Plans were executed between 1966 and 1969. This period also saw the devaluation of the Rupee and the initiation of the Green Revolution strategy. 1978-80 saw the Rolling Plan (Janata Govt). 1990-92 saw another break due to political instability and economic crisis, with two annual plans. PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CGL, RRB NTPC, UPSC Prelims.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The concept of "Rolling Plan" in India was introduced by which government and during which period?

options.option_text: The Janata Party government during 1978-80
The Congress government during 1966-69
The National Front government during 1990-92
The NDA government during 1998-99

questions.explanation: ROLLING PLAN (1978-1980): The Janata Party government under Morarji Desai terminated the Fifth Five Year Plan a year early (in 1978) and introduced the "Rolling Plan" concept (formulated by Gunnar Myrdal). A rolling plan means the plan is revised at the end of every year, updating targets and allocations. However, the Janata government fell, and the returning Congress government under Indira Gandhi discarded the Rolling Plan and launched the Sixth Five Year Plan in 1980. PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CGL, State PSCs.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Which Five-Year Plan recognized "Human Development" as the core of all developmental efforts and marked India's transition towards indicative planning?

options.option_text: Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-1997)
Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-1985)
Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-2007)
Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-1974)

questions.explanation: EIGHTH PLAN (1992-1997): Launched after the 1991 economic reforms (LPG). It shifted planning in India from imperative/directive planning to INDICATIVE PLANNING (government provides direction, market forces execute). It explicitly recognized Human Development (education, health) as the ultimate goal of development. It was highly successful, achieving a growth rate of 6.8% against a target of 5.6%. Often associated with the Rao-Manmohan model. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims, State PSCs.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The "Gadgil Formula", used for allocating central plan assistance to states, was first introduced during the formulation of which Five-Year Plan?

options.option_text: Fourth Five Year Plan
Second Five Year Plan
Eighth Five Year Plan
Tenth Five Year Plan

questions.explanation: GADGIL FORMULA: Formulated by D.R. Gadgil, then Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission, in 1969 for the FOURTH FIVE YEAR PLAN. Before this, central assistance to states was schematic and lacked an objective criteria. The formula distributed funds based on Population (60%), Per Capita Income (10%), Tax Effort (10%), Ongoing Irrigation/Power projects (10%), and Special Problems (10%). It was later modified into the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims, State PSCs.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Which Five-Year Plan was launched with the specific theme of "Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth"?

options.option_text: Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-2017)
Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-2012)
Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-2007)
Ninth Five Year Plan (1997-2002)

questions.explanation: TWELFTH PLAN (2012-2017): This was India's last Five-Year Plan before the Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog. Its central theme was "Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth". The ELEVENTH PLAN's theme was simply "Faster and More Inclusive Growth" — the 12th plan added the word "Sustainable", emphasizing environmental sustainability. The plan targeted 8% GDP growth. PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CGL, RRB.

questions.stem: The slogan "Garibi Hatao" (Eradicate Poverty) was famously associated with which Five-Year Plan?

options.option_text: Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-1979)
Third Five Year Plan (1961-1966)
Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-1985)
Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-1974)

questions.explanation: GARIBI HATAO: The slogan was coined by Indira Gandhi during the 1971 elections. The subsequent FIFTH FIVE YEAR PLAN (1974-1979) was the first to explicitly make poverty alleviation and self-reliance its two main objectives. The plan introduced the Minimum Needs Programme (MNP). Note: The Twenty-Point Programme was also launched during this period (1975). PYQ FREQUENCY: Very high in SSC, Railways, State PSCs.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The First Five Year Plan (1951–56) was anchored to which economic model, and which sector received the highest budgetary allocation?

options.option_text: Mahalanobis model, with heavy industries receiving the largest share
Harrod-Domar model, with agriculture and irrigation as the priority sector
Feldman model, focused on capital goods and core industrial sectors
Leontief input-output model, emphasising balanced multi-sectoral growth

questions.explanation: B is correct: the First FYP used the Harrod-Domar growth model and directed its largest allocation (~44%) to agriculture, land reform, and irrigation to tackle food shortage left by Partition. Option A is wrong because the Mahalanobis model drove the Second FYP, not the First.

questions.stem: The 'Minimum Needs Programme (MNP)'—covering elementary education, rural health, and rural drinking water supply—was first incorporated as a distinct programme component in which Five Year Plan?

options.option_text: Third Five Year Plan (1961–66), centred on the self-reliance objective
Fourth Five Year Plan (1969–74), formulated under Indira Gandhi's leadership
Fifth Five Year Plan (1974–79), which also stressed direct poverty removal
Sixth Five Year Plan (1980–85), which universalised IRDP across all districts

questions.explanation: C is correct: the Fifth FYP (1974–79), drafted under D.D. Dhar, introduced the MNP to ensure baseline public services reached the rural poor. Option D is a common trap because IRDP was universalised in the Sixth Plan—but MNP itself began in the Fifth.

questions.stem: The Seventh Five Year Plan (1985–90) was built around which central slogan that encapsulated its three strategic priorities for development?

options.option_text: Equity, efficiency, and environmental sustainability for the nation
Food, work, and productivity across all sectors of the economy
Poverty removal, employment generation, and industrial self-reliance
Growth with social justice and rapid modernisation of infrastructure

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Seventh FYP explicitly adopted 'Food, Work, and Productivity' as its theme, focusing on foodgrain sufficiency, rural employment, and raising factor productivity. Option C describes the broader rhetoric of the Fifth FYP ('Garibi Hatao' era), not the Seventh.

questions.stem: India's Planning Commission, constituted in March 1950 as the apex body for national economic planning, derived its legal authority from which source?

options.option_text: An Act of Parliament enacted under Article 246 of the Constitution
A Union Cabinet resolution, making it an extra-constitutional advisory body
A Presidential Ordinance issued under emergency provisions of the Constitution
A Constituent Assembly directive embedded in the Directive Principles text

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Planning Commission was set up purely by an executive (Cabinet) resolution—it had no statutory backing and is therefore called an extra-constitutional body. Option A is wrong because no Parliamentary legislation ever created it, which is why it could also be dissolved by a Cabinet decision (as happened in 2014).

questions.stem: Which Five Year Plan was the first to set an explicit GDP growth rate target of 8 per cent per annum, signalling India's intent to accelerate toward high-growth East Asian benchmarks?

options.option_text: Eighth Five Year Plan (1992–97), launched after economic liberalisation
Ninth Five Year Plan (1997–2002), under the National Democratic Alliance
Tenth Five Year Plan (2002–07), approved under PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee
Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007–12), drafted under the UPA-I government

questions.explanation: C is correct: the Tenth FYP was the first to target 8% annual GDP growth; earlier plans had more modest targets (8th Plan ≈5.6%, 9th Plan ≈6.5%). Option D is a common mistake because the Eleventh Plan also targeted 9%, but the 8% barrier was first crossed in the Tenth Plan.

questions.stem: The Third Five Year Plan (1961–66) is widely regarded as a 'crisis plan' that failed to meet its targets. Which combination of external and domestic shocks was primarily responsible for its derailment?

options.option_text: Sino-Indian War (1962), Indo-Pak War (1965), and the severe drought of 1965–66
Bangladesh Liberation War (1971), global oil price shock (1973), and 1966 famine
Emergency declaration (1975), bank nationalisation (1969), and drought of 1966
Korean War commodity-price surge (1951), drought (1965–66), and oil shock (1973)

questions.explanation: A is correct: the Third FYP was hit by three overlapping crises—defence expenditure spikes from the 1962 Sino-Indian War and 1965 Indo-Pak War diverted planned resources, while the 1965–66 droughts caused foodgrain shortfalls and a foreign-exchange crisis. Options B and C embed events from later plans; the oil shock (Option D) belongs to the 1973–74 period affecting the Fifth Plan.

questions.stem: The Mahalanobis heavy-industry model underpinning the Second Five Year Plan faced a significant academic challenge. Economists C.N. Vakil and P.R. Brahmananda argued for an alternative strategy—what was the core proposition of their counter-model?

options.option_text: Growth should be led by export promotion and foreign exchange earnings accumulation
Expanding output of wage goods (mass-consumption goods) was the faster path to employment
Free-market price signals without state intervention would maximise industrial output
Human capital investment through mass education must precede physical capital formation

questions.explanation: B is correct: Vakil and Brahmananda's 'Wage Goods Model' held that investment in consumer goods consumed by wage earners (food, cloth, footwear) would create purchasing power and self-sustaining employment cycles faster than heavy-industry investment. Option C describes B.R. Shenoy's free-market critique—a different, contemporaneous dissent—which is the most plausible distractor.
